newsitem.title: UK: UK beet crop needs rain, some factory delays noted.
newsitem.headline: UK beet crop needs rain, some factory delays noted.

text.p: Britain still looks to be on course for improved sugar production from its beet crop this year despite a lack of moisture and operational problems in some of the processing factories, beet experts said on Tuesday.
"The crop is still continuing to grow quite nicely with this balmy spell of weather. This autumn weather is ideal for late beet development," said an official at British Sugar.
"The general picture is that while the harvest is proceeding fairly well, a drop of rain wouldn't go amiss right across the whole beet growing area."
More rain would also help soften soil for lifting beets.
The current mild weather could tempt farmers to keep beets a little longer in the ground, the official added.
British Sugar has yet to release interim statistics on numbers of beets lifted and clamped.

But a spokeswoman for the National Farmers Union (NFU) said while prospects for this year's crop had improved, there were still problems with some of the processing factories -- such as boiler trouble -- causing them to open later than scheduled.
"The crop is a lot better than anyone expected and the factories are having problems, which has not helped," she said, adding that some beets had been diverted to other plants.

"The upshot is that they have reduced slice capacity on beet which will frustrate growers because they have lifted in preparation to deliver quantities of beet under permit, which now they can't do. So everything is waiting around on the farm."
But the British Sugar official was more optimistic, saying the campaign was running smoothly.
"The stuff is coming out, the beet is going to the factories and the factories are going well," he said.

Sugar contents in beet from this year's crop are reported to have reached 19 percent in some cases, which has hampered sugar production as factory machinery is optimised to process beets with contents at around 17.5 percent, the NFU spokeswoman said.
"Sugar contents have been quite high which has restricted the factories' ability to process," she said.
The combination of delaying factors was likely to cause a long campaign this year, which in turn could delay sowings of other crops such as wheat, she added.

Czarnikow Sugar has estimated Britain's 1996/97 sugar output at 1.36 million tonnes raw value, slightly higher than the 1.33 million tonnes turned out in the previous crop year. The area sown to beet has been estimated at 170,000 hectares.
